options.a: Known latent defects or conditions that could significantly affect value or desirability
options.b: The seller's reasons for selling and the lowest price the seller is willing to accept
options.c: The racial or religious makeup of the neighborhood surrounding the property
options.d: That a former occupant of the home was living with HIV or AIDS

distractorExplanations.b: Seller motivation and bottom-line price are confidential client information, not material property facts.
distractorExplanations.c: Discussing neighborhood racial or religious composition is steering under the Fair Housing Act, not a required disclosure.
distractorExplanations.d: HIV/AIDS is a protected disability under federal fair housing law; it is not a material property fact to disclose.

pa-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Material property defects and legally required disclosures must be shared; confidential motivations may be protected. Disclosure duties follow applicable law.

options.a: Inheritance
options.b: Homestead
options.c: Reversion
options.d: Survivorship

distractorExplanations.a: Confuses joint tenancy with tenancy in common; a joint tenant's interest passes to co-owners, not heirs.
distractorExplanations.b: Homestead is a separate protection of a residence from certain creditors, not a feature of joint tenancy.
distractorExplanations.c: Reversion is the grantor's future interest after a life estate, unrelated to co-ownership rights.

options.a: Land bordering a lake, sea, or ocean with still or tidal water
options.b: Rights to minerals, oil, and gas beneath the land's surface
options.c: Land bordering flowing water such as a river or stream
options.d: Rights to use the airspace above the land for development

distractorExplanations.a: Rights along lakes, seas, and oceans are littoral rights; riparian rights concern flowing rivers and streams.
distractorExplanations.b: Subsurface mineral rights are a separate bundle of rights and are unrelated to water boundaries.
distractorExplanations.d: Air rights cover space above the land and can be severed, but they are not water rights.

options.a: A VA loan is made with zero down payment
options.b: Conventional LTV is low (commonly below 80%)
options.c: The seller pays two discount points at closing
options.d: Conventional LTV is high (commonly above 80%)

distractorExplanations.a: VA loans charge a funding fee instead of PMI; PMI applies to conventional loans with thin equity.
distractorExplanations.b: Reverses the threshold: PMI is required when LTV is above 80%, and it can be dropped once equity reaches 20%.
distractorExplanations.c: Discount points buy down the interest rate; who pays them has nothing to do with whether PMI is required.

options.a: Public use and the owner's consent
options.b: Payment of the property's assessed value
options.c: A police-power finding without compensation
options.d: Public use/purpose and just compensation

distractorExplanations.a: Eminent domain is a forced taking; the owner's consent is not required, which is what distinguishes condemnation from a voluntary sale.
distractorExplanations.b: Just compensation is based on fair market value, not the tax assessor's assessed value, which is often lower.
distractorExplanations.c: Confuses eminent domain with police power: zoning and code regulation need no compensation, but a taking does.

pa-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Takings require public use/purpose and just compensation under the Fifth Amendment (constitutional framework).

options.a: A claim, encumbrance, or defect that may impair marketability
options.b: A zoning variance granted to the owner for a hardship use
options.c: A deed recorded with a full covenant of warranty from the grantor
options.d: The abstract summary of the chain of title prepared for a buyer

distractorExplanations.b: Confuses public land-use control with title: a variance governs permitted use and is not a claim against ownership.
distractorExplanations.c: A recorded general warranty deed strengthens the chain of title; it is the opposite of a cloud that casts doubt on it.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses an abstract of title (a history of recorded documents) with a cloud, which is a defect or claim the abstract may reveal.

options.a: 1% of the loan amount
options.b: 1% of the purchase price
options.c: 1% of the down payment
options.d: 1% of the interest rate

distractorExplanations.b: Points are computed on the loan amount, not the price; on a $200,000 price with a $160,000 loan, one point is $1,600.
distractorExplanations.c: Uses the wrong base: the down payment is the buyer's equity, while points are a percentage of the amount borrowed.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses one point (1% of the loan amount) with one percentage point of interest rate; a point typically buys down far less.

options.a: Obtain the highest price by carrying out every seller instruction, lawful or not
options.b: Owe the buyer customer the same loyalty and confidentiality as the seller
options.c: Guarantee the seller a closed sale at list price within the listing term
options.d: Promote the seller's interests with loyalty, care, and obedience within the law

distractorExplanations.a: Obedience extends only to lawful instructions; a broker must refuse illegal directions such as discriminatory or fraudulent ones.
distractorExplanations.b: Confuses client and customer: a buyer customer is owed honesty and fair dealing, not the fiduciary loyalty owed to the seller client.
distractorExplanations.c: Fiduciary duties concern conduct (loyalty, care, obedience), not guaranteed outcomes; brokers cannot promise a sale or price.

options.a: Agreed orally to buy land without a writing
options.b: Signed without having the contract notarized
options.c: Was induced by fraud or was a minor
options.d: Agreed with the other party to an illegal purpose

distractorExplanations.a: An oral land contract is unenforceable under the statute of frauds, which is different from voidable at one party's option.
distractorExplanations.b: Notarization is not required for a contract to be valid; lack of a notary does not give a party the power to void it.
distractorExplanations.d: A contract for an illegal purpose is void from the start, not voidable at the option of one protected party.

pa-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Fraud or lack of capacity can make a contract voidable by the protected party (depending on circumstances).

options.a: The broker's compensation is the amount above a seller's net price
options.b: The broker's compensation is a fixed percentage of the final sale price
options.c: The seller keeps the right to sell on their own without owing a commission
options.d: The broker's flat fee is owed up front even if the property does not sell

distractorExplanations.b: That describes a standard percentage commission listing, which does not create the net listing's incentive to underprice.
distractorExplanations.c: That describes an exclusive agency listing, not a net listing where the broker keeps everything above the seller's net.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses a net listing with a flat-fee or advance-fee arrangement; a net listing pays the broker only the excess over the net price.

pa-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Net listings pay the broker the amount above the seller's net price, creating conflict-of-interest concerns: they can incentivize underpricing and are banned or tightly regulated in many places.

options.a: Mixing client trust money with personal or operating funds improperly
options.b: Spending client trust money on the broker's personal or business expenses
options.c: Holding several clients' earnest money deposits in one trust account
options.d: Depositing earnest money later than the deadline set by license law

distractorExplanations.b: Using trust money for the broker's own purposes is conversion, a separate and more serious violation than commingling.
distractorExplanations.c: Pooling multiple clients' funds in one properly maintained trust account is permitted; mixing with broker funds is the problem.
distractorExplanations.d: A late deposit is a separate trust-account violation; commingling is mixing trust money with personal or operating funds.

options.a: At the closing table, when the settlement statement is reviewed
options.b: Once an offer is accepted, so negotiations are not disrupted
options.c: After the agreement of sale is signed, in a written addendum to the contract
options.d: Before or as soon as practicable when the dual/designated relationship arises

distractorExplanations.a: Closing is far too late; the parties must know about dual or designated agency before they rely on the licensee.
distractorExplanations.b: Disclosing after acceptance means the parties negotiated without knowing the relationship; disclosure comes first.
distractorExplanations.c: An addendum after signing comes too late; disclosure is required before or as soon as the dual relationship arises.

pa-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Agency disclosure timing is early—when the dual or designated relationship is created or contemplated. Applicable state rules set the exact form.

options.a: The listing broker is owed a commission if the property sells during the term, regardless of who finds the buyer
options.b: The listing broker earns a commission if the property sells during the term, unless the seller personally finds the buyer
options.c: The seller may list with several brokers at once and pays a commission only to the broker who produces the buyer
options.d: The listing broker may sell the property to any buyer without the seller's approval of the price or terms

distractorExplanations.b: That describes an exclusive agency listing, where the seller keeps the right to sell without commission.
distractorExplanations.c: That describes an open listing; exclusive right-to-sell gives one broker the commission on any sale during the term.
distractorExplanations.d: A listing hires the broker to find a buyer; it does not give the broker authority to accept offers or bind the seller.

pa-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Exclusive right-to-sell typically protects the listing broker's commission if a sale occurs during the listing term. The exact terms are set by the listing agreement.

options.a: Suggest an offer amount, since the seller benefits from a fast sale
options.b: Share the seller's lowest acceptable price so the buyer offers fairly
options.c: Advise on offer price once the buyer signs the Consumer Notice as a customer
options.d: Avoid acting as the buyer's advocate and stay within the listing agency role

distractorExplanations.a: Advising the buyer on price is advocacy for the buyer and conflicts with the listing agent's duties to the seller.
distractorExplanations.b: Disclosing the seller's bottom line breaches confidentiality owed to the seller client.
distractorExplanations.c: The Consumer Notice discloses relationships; it does not create buyer agency or permit buyer price advocacy.

pa-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Listing agents represent the seller; advocacy for a buyer requires a proper agency shift/disclosure. Buyer advocacy requires properly creating buyer agency where allowed.

options.a: Deadlines apply to the closing date but not to contingency periods
options.b: Contract dates and times are critical and late performance may be a breach
options.c: Late performance is excused if the late party gives written notice before the deadline
options.d: Parties must close within 30 days of signing the agreement of sale

distractorExplanations.a: The clause makes all stated contract dates material, including inspection and financing contingency deadlines.
distractorExplanations.c: Notice does not extend a deadline; extensions require a written agreement of both parties.
distractorExplanations.d: The clause enforces the dates the parties chose; it does not impose a 30-day closing period.

options.a: An obligation to buy on stated terms within a period
options.b: Equitable title to the property from the date the option is signed
options.c: A right of first refusal to match any later third-party offer
options.d: A right to purchase on stated terms within a period

distractorExplanations.a: The optionee has a right, not an obligation; only the optionor is bound to sell if the option is exercised.
distractorExplanations.b: Equitable title passes to a buyer under a sales contract or land contract, not to an optionee before exercise.
distractorExplanations.c: A right of first refusal depends on the owner deciding to sell; an option fixes the terms the optionee may buy on.

pa-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: An option is a purchased right, not an obligation, to buy on fixed terms for a time. The right is usually purchased for consideration.

options.a: Exaggerated opinion that a reasonable person would not treat as a factual warranty
options.b: A false statement of a measurable fact, such as lot size or year built
options.c: Prohibited advertising that the Commission treats as misrepresentation
options.d: An opinion the licensee must support with a written CMA before publishing it in an ad

distractorExplanations.b: Misstating a measurable fact is misrepresentation, the opposite of puffing, which is vague opinion.
distractorExplanations.c: Puffing is generally lawful opinion; it becomes a problem only when it crosses into false statements of fact.
distractorExplanations.d: A CMA supports pricing; vague opinions such as 'charming' or 'stunning views' need no data support.

options.a: Practicing law whenever they fill in any blank on a standard form
options.b: Required to have the buyer's attorney approve each completed blank
options.c: Practicing law if they draft novel legal clauses beyond authorized forms
options.d: Shielded from liability for errors because the form was drafted by the association

distractorExplanations.a: Filling in approved forms is permitted; unauthorized practice of law arises from drafting new legal language.
distractorExplanations.b: Attorney review is optional unless a contract says otherwise; licensees may complete approved forms.
distractorExplanations.d: A standard form does not protect a licensee from negligence in completing it.

options.a: Not create the dual agency relationship; consider designated agency, referral, or withdrawal
options.b: Proceed as a dual agent after giving the seller written notice of the relationship
options.c: Proceed as a dual agent if the buyer consents in writing, since one party's consent is enough
options.d: Convert to a transaction licensee role, which needs no agreement from either party

distractorExplanations.b: Notice is not consent; where consent is required, a refusal means no dual agency.
distractorExplanations.c: Dual agency needs both clients' informed consent; buyer consent alone cannot override the seller's refusal.
distractorExplanations.d: A transaction licensee relationship also needs a written agreement; it cannot be imposed on a seller who refused.

pa-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Consent is required for dual agency where the model is used; without it, other compliant paths are needed. Choose the compliant alternative that fits the situation.

options.a: Upon the death of the remainderman
options.b: When the life tenant sells the interest
options.c: When the life tenant moves out of the home
options.d: Upon the death of the measuring life

distractorExplanations.a: The remainderman's death does not end the life estate; the remainder passes to the remainderman's heirs.
distractorExplanations.b: A life tenant can convey the interest, but the buyer's estate still ends at the measuring life's death.
distractorExplanations.c: A life estate is a freehold interest; vacating the property does not terminate it.

pa-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Life estates are measured by a life; remainder/reversion follows. The grant may also define another measuring life or ending event.

options.a: Must take title at the same time and by the same deed
options.b: Pass their shares to the surviving co-owners at death
options.c: Must hold equal shares but may convey them without consent
options.d: May hold unequal shares and typically lack survivorship

distractorExplanations.a: Unity of time and title is a joint tenancy requirement; tenants in common may acquire at different times.
distractorExplanations.b: That is the right of survivorship, the defining feature of joint tenancy, not tenancy in common.
distractorExplanations.c: Equal shares are required for joint tenancy; tenants in common may hold unequal interests.

pa-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: TIC allows unequal interests and no automatic survivorship. Survivorship applies only if specified.

options.a: Rezoning of one parcel to a different district
options.b: Permission to deviate from a zoning requirement due to hardship
options.c: Permission for a use the ordinance allows only after a special review
options.d: Permission to keep a use that existed before the current ordinance

distractorExplanations.a: Rezoning a single parcel is a map amendment (sometimes spot zoning), not a variance from a requirement.
distractorExplanations.c: That describes a special exception or conditional use permit, not a hardship variance.
distractorExplanations.d: That is a nonconforming use (grandfathered), not a variance.

pa-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Variances grant relief from strict zoning application in hardship cases. It is granted by the zoning authority.

options.a: Recording the deed in the public land records
options.b: Delivering the signed deed to the grantee
options.c: Having the deed notarized by a licensed notary
options.d: Taking physical possession of the property

distractorExplanations.b: Delivery and acceptance transfer title between the parties but do not give notice to the world.
distractorExplanations.c: Acknowledgment makes a deed eligible for recording; notarization alone gives no public notice.
distractorExplanations.d: Possession gives actual or inquiry notice, not the constructive notice that recording provides.

options.a: Loan amount ÷ (purchase price − down payment) × 100%
options.b: Loan amount ÷ appraised value (or purchase price) × 100%
options.c: Down payment ÷ appraised value (or purchase price) × 100%
options.d: Monthly housing payment ÷ gross monthly income × 100%

distractorExplanations.a: Subtracting the down payment from the denominator understates value and overstates the LTV.
distractorExplanations.c: Down payment over value is the equity percentage, the complement of LTV.
distractorExplanations.d: That is the front-end (housing) debt-to-income ratio, not loan-to-value.

pa-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: LTV ratios loan size to property value. Lenders typically use the lower of appraised value or purchase price.

options.a: Interest only, with the full principal due as a balloon at maturity
options.b: Principal first, with interest paid after the balance is cleared
options.c: Interest and principal in equal amounts every month of the term
options.d: Both interest and principal so the balance declines over the term

distractorExplanations.a: That describes an interest-only or balloon loan, not a fully amortizing mortgage.
distractorExplanations.b: Interest accrues on the outstanding balance and is paid with each installment; early payments are mostly interest.
distractorExplanations.c: The payment is level, but the split shifts from mostly interest toward mostly principal over time.

options.a: Capping the interest rate lenders may charge on residential loans
options.b: Banning certain kickbacks and requiring settlement cost disclosures
options.c: Requiring lenders to disclose the APR on all consumer credit
options.d: Prohibiting lending discrimination based on race or national origin

distractorExplanations.a: Interest-rate ceilings come from state usury laws, not RESPA.
distractorExplanations.c: APR disclosure comes from the Truth in Lending Act (Regulation Z), not RESPA.
distractorExplanations.d: That is the Equal Credit Opportunity Act and Fair Housing Act, not RESPA.

pa-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: RESPA addresses settlement services, kickbacks, and related disclosures (with TRID integration for many loans). It applies to covered federally related mortgage transactions.

options.a: Requires extra payment if the borrower pays off early
options.b: Charges a fee when the borrower makes a payment after the grace period
options.c: Lets the lender call the loan due on sale
options.d: Raises the interest rate if the borrower defaults on the note

distractorExplanations.b: That is a late charge for overdue payments, not a penalty for paying the loan off early.
distractorExplanations.c: That is a due-on-sale (alienation) clause, which accelerates the debt on transfer.
distractorExplanations.d: That describes a default-rate provision, not a charge for early payoff.

pa-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: Prepayment penalties charge for early payoff when permitted by the loan terms and law. It applies only when the note and applicable law allow it.

options.a: Can adjust based on the lender's margin alone, with no index
options.b: Resets annually to the current prime rate with no caps
options.c: Can adjust based on an index plus margin, subject to caps
options.d: Adjusts based on the borrower's credit score at each reset

distractorExplanations.a: The margin is fixed for the loan; the change comes from the published index the margin is added to.
distractorExplanations.b: ARMs follow the index named in the note and normally have periodic and lifetime caps.
distractorExplanations.d: Credit score affects initial pricing; later adjustments follow the index plus margin.

options.a: Defects in the structure found after the home inspection
options.b: Lender losses when the borrower defaults
options.c: Survey and boundary defects under a standard owner's policy
options.d: Covered title defects and claims against ownership

distractorExplanations.a: Physical defects are a property-condition issue, not a title risk; title insurance covers ownership defects.
distractorExplanations.b: Default risk is covered by mortgage insurance (PMI/FHA MIP), not title insurance.
distractorExplanations.c: Standard policies usually exclude matters an accurate survey would reveal unless extended coverage is purchased.

pa-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: Owner's/lender's title policies insure against covered title risks, not casualty. Coverage follows the terms and exclusions of the policy.

options.a: The buyer receives a credit that reduces cash to close
options.b: The buyer is charged; it increases cash needed
options.c: The lender pays the item at closing
options.d: The item is split evenly between buyer and seller

distractorExplanations.a: That describes a credit to the buyer; a debit is a charge that increases the amount the buyer brings.
distractorExplanations.c: A debit charges the named party; lender-paid items show as credits to the buyer.
distractorExplanations.d: Prorated items are split by days owed, and a debit shows only the buyer's charged share.

pa-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-c.explanation: Debits charge a party; buyer debits typically increase funds due at closing. For a seller, a debit reduces sale proceeds.

options.a: Buy and sell existing mortgages, improving liquidity for originators
options.b: Make loans directly to borrowers who cannot qualify with banks
options.c: Insure lenders against borrower default on loans with low down payments
options.d: Set the federal funds rate that lenders use to price new loans

distractorExplanations.b: Lending directly to borrowers is the primary market; the secondary market buys loans already made.
distractorExplanations.c: Default insurance comes from PMI or FHA, not the secondary market's loan purchases.
distractorExplanations.d: The Federal Reserve sets the federal funds target, not Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, or other secondary-market buyers.

options.a: Maximum interest rates that may be charged on certain loans
options.b: Minimum down payments a lender must require on certain loans
options.c: Disclosure of the APR before a loan is consummated
options.d: Maximum loan amounts a lender may make on certain properties

distractorExplanations.b: Down-payment minimums come from loan programs and underwriting, not usury statutes.
distractorExplanations.c: APR disclosure is a Truth in Lending Act requirement; usury laws cap the rate itself.
distractorExplanations.d: Loan limits come from conforming-loan or FHA program rules, not usury caps on interest.

options.a: Fund construction draws that convert to a permanent mortgage once the home is completed
options.b: Finance a short-term gap between purchase of a new home and sale of an existing one
options.c: Fund a 30-year fully amortizing primary residence as the only permanent loan
options.d: Cover the down payment through a second loan closed with the first mortgage

distractorExplanations.a: That describes a construction-to-permanent loan, not short-term bridge financing between two homes.
distractorExplanations.d: That describes a piggyback second mortgage (such as 80-10-10), not a bridge loan.
distractorExplanations.c: That is a permanent mortgage.

options.a: A licensing-board matter in which the state commission orders who receives the fee
options.b: A civil/contract matter between the brokers (or via MLS/association processes)
options.c: Grounds for the listing broker to hold the buyer's deposit until the fee is paid
options.d: A matter the closing agent settles by splitting the fee equally

distractorExplanations.a: Real estate commissions discipline licensees but do not adjudicate fee splits between brokers; that is a contract matter or association arbitration.
distractorExplanations.c: Earnest money belongs to the transaction and follows escrow rules; a broker-to-broker fee dispute is not a lawful reason to withhold it.
distractorExplanations.d: Closing agents disburse per instructions and agreements; they have no authority to resolve a commission dispute by splitting the fee.

pa-real-estate-readiness-check-pa-licens.explanation: Commission disputes are between licensees/firms; earnest money still follows contract/escrow rules. It is not a reason to withhold a buyer's earnest money unlawfully.

options.a: Is granted on request to any licensee holding an active license in a bordering state
options.b: Requires retaking the full national and state exams with no waiver possible
options.c: Is handled under a federal multistate license issued by HUD
options.d: Depends on Commission rules, education/exam waivers, and any state-portion steps

distractorExplanations.a: Neighbouring-state licensure does not by itself confer a license; recognition follows the commission's specific agreements and application steps.
distractorExplanations.b: Recognition pathways commonly waive the national portion or education; requiring a full retake with no waiver overstates the burden.
distractorExplanations.c: There is no federal real estate license; HUD does not license brokers, and recognition is a state commission decision.

options.a: Release it to the seller as liquidated damages
options.b: Follow authorized escrow dispute procedures
options.c: Split it evenly between buyer and seller
options.d: Apply it toward the brokerage's earned commission

distractorExplanations.a: Treating the deposit as forfeited is a unilateral award; the broker must use release, interpleader, or other authorized procedures instead.
distractorExplanations.c: An even split is still a unilateral decision on disputed funds; the broker needs a signed release or a court/authorized dispute process.
distractorExplanations.d: Taking disputed trust money as commission is conversion of escrow funds; the broker cannot pay itself from a disputed deposit.

pa-real-estate-readiness-check-pa-licens.explanation: Escrow disputes require contractual and regulatory procedures (interpleader, releases, etc.) The broker does not unilaterally award the funds to either party.

options.a: May not engage in activities requiring an active license until renewed/reactivated
options.b: May keep showing homes and writing offers during a renewal grace period
options.c: May continue practicing as long as the missed CE hours are finished before the next renewal
options.d: May keep practicing under the supervising broker's license until reinstated

distractorExplanations.b: A late-renewal period only allows reinstatement with fees; licensed activity is not permitted while the license is inactive or expired.
distractorExplanations.c: Completing CE later does not cure inactive status now; the license must be renewed or reactivated before any licensed activity.
distractorExplanations.d: A broker's license does not cover an affiliate whose own license is inactive; each licensee needs an active license to practice.

options.a: Permitted once the listing agreement has expired
options.b: A serious breach of fiduciary/license duties
options.c: Allowed if the licensee offers full list price
options.d: Only an issue if the seller later sues

distractorExplanations.a: The duty not to misuse a client's confidential information survives the end of the listing; expiry does not license self-dealing.
distractorExplanations.c: Paying list price does not cure undisclosed self-dealing or the misuse of confidential information about the client's position.
distractorExplanations.d: Undisclosed self-dealing is a license-law violation the commission can discipline on its own, whether or not the seller sues.

options.a: Allowed if the ad includes the agent's phone number
options.b: Permitted on social media but not in print ads
options.c: Allowed for teaser ads that run under 30 days
options.d: Prohibited or restricted by advertising rules

distractorExplanations.a: A phone number alone does not identify the licensed brokerage; advertising rules require the firm name or licensed status to be shown.
distractorExplanations.b: Advertising rules apply to online and social media ads the same way as print; the platform does not create a blind-ad exception.
distractorExplanations.c: There is no short-run or teaser exception; any licensee advertisement must disclose the brokerage identity from the start.

options.a: Subject to advertising and inducement rules
options.b: Allowed if the car is given only after closing
options.c: Treated as a lawful rebate needing no disclosure
options.d: Permitted for sellers but banned for buyers

distractorExplanations.b: Delaying the prize until closing does not take it outside inducement rules; terms and conditions still have to be disclosed clearly.
distractorExplanations.c: A prize offer is regulated as an inducement and advertising claim; calling it a rebate does not remove the disclosure requirements.
distractorExplanations.d: Inducement rules are not split by party type; the same advertising and disclosure standards apply to offers aimed at sellers or buyers.

pa-real-estate-readiness-check-pa-licens.explanation: Inducements are regulated; deceptive or prohibited prizes can trigger discipline. They may be restricted or require clear disclosure of terms.

options.a: A 90-day grace period during which practice continues as normal
options.b: Loss of all prior CE credit and a mandatory retake of the national exam
options.c: Late fees, inactive status, or other penalties until cured
options.d: A one-time warning letter with no fee for a first late filing

distractorExplanations.a: A late period may allow reinstatement with fees, but licensed activity is not authorized while the renewal is lapsed.
distractorExplanations.b: Late renewal triggers fees and status changes; an exam retake is typically tied to long lapses, not a short late filing.
distractorExplanations.d: Late-renewal consequences are set by rule (fees, inactive status); there is no standard free first-offence warning.

options.a: Allowed if the agent stays on the phone throughout
options.b: Improper and a security/agency violation risk
options.c: Acceptable if the home is vacant and listed
options.d: Allowed for a preview before the listing goes live

distractorExplanations.a: Remote phone contact does not supervise access or create seller authorization; the unlicensed person is still entering without consent.
distractorExplanations.c: Vacancy does not reduce the seller's authority over access; unauthorized entry to a vacant listing is still a security and agency breach.
distractorExplanations.d: Pre-market timing does not change the rule; lockbox access is limited to authorized licensees with the seller's permission.

options.a: Be registered/comply with branch office rules when required
options.b: Hold a separate corporate broker license independent of the main office
options.c: Be managed by any licensed salesperson the main broker chooses
options.d: Operate under a franchise name without listing the main brokerage

distractorExplanations.b: A branch operates under the main brokerage's license and supervision; it is not a separately licensed independent firm.
distractorExplanations.c: Branch supervision must meet the manager/broker qualification rules; an ordinary salesperson cannot run a branch on the broker's say-so.
distractorExplanations.d: Advertising and signage must identify the licensed brokerage; a franchise trade name alone does not satisfy the identification rule.
